name: Sprocket
text:
DO: Adopt a version-controlled system for prompts, engines, and routing rules.

This keeps every change tracked with clear authorship and timestamps, making it easy to audit and roll back mistakes. The trade-off is that version control requires discipline to write useful commit messages—skip that and the log becomes noise, same as a shared log.

name: Gauge
text: A shared log buries decisions under noise—no discipline, no rollback, no way to tell which changes mattered. Version control forces clarity: each commit must justify itself, and Git’s history lets us undo mistakes. Settle it by running a 2-week pilot: log changes both ways, then compare how long it takes to answer “Why did X break?”—the version-controlled system will win.
